questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis with clean base and raised rolled edges for 3 weeks. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is non-tender. What is the most appropriate initial investigation?
opts: Dark field microscopy of serous exudate
questions.exp: The clinical description is classic primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre). Dark field microscopy of serous exudate from the ulcer base is the gold standard for direct visualisation of Treponema pallidum spirochaetes before serological tests turn positive.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 count 80 cells/µL) develops multiple painless pearly papules with central umbilication on the face and trunk. Histology shows intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies filling the entire cytoplasm. Which of the following best describes the causative agent?
opts: Herpesvirus with latency in dorsal root ganglia
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscipoxvirus (poxvirus family), affecting only humans. The characteristic Henderson-Patterson bodies are large intracytoplasmic inclusions. It is more widespread and recalcitrant in immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A 22-year-old female presents with erythematous scaly plaques on the scalp extending beyond the hairline, pitting of nails (thimble-like), and Auspitz sign. Which cytokine axis is the primary therapeutic target in her condition?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is primarily driven by the IL-23/Th17 axis. IL-23 promotes differentiation of Th17 cells, which produce IL-17A. Biologics targeting IL-17A (secukinumab, ixekizumab) and IL-23 (guselkumab, risankizumab) are now first-line for moderate-to-severe psoriasis.

questions.q: A 50-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset painful erythematous nodules on the face, forearms and thighs with high fever and joint pain. His biopsy shows diffuse dermal infiltration with foamy macrophages and leukocyte infiltration in vessel walls. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction occurring in lepromatous/borderline lepromatous leprosy. It is immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). Tender nodules, fever, and systemic features distinguish it from Type 1 (reversal) reactions which are cell-mediated and cause upgrading of skin lesions.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. ELISA detects antibodies against BP180 and BP230. Which cell type is crucial in blister formation in this disease?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterised by autoantibodies against BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. Eosinophils are the key effector cells — they degranulate releasing MMP-9 and elastase which cleave the hemidesmosomal anchoring complex, causing subepidermal blistering.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the perianal area with burning pain and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. He had a similar episode 3 months ago. Which investigation confirms the aetiological diagnosis most rapidly?
opts: Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells
questions.exp: While Tzanck smear is rapid, it cannot distinguish HSV-1 from HSV-2 and has lower sensitivity. PCR for HSV DNA is the gold standard — most sensitive and specific, distinguishes HSV-1 from HSV-2, and gives results within hours from vesicle swabs or CSF.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a painless papule that evolved into an ulcer with undermined violaceous edges on the lower leg over 6 months. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with granulomas containing copper-coloured, thick-walled, round sclerotic bodies with cross-walls. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous fungi (most commonly Fonsecaea pedrosoi in India). The pathognomonic finding is Medlar bodies (muriform cells/sclerotic bodies) — brown, thick-walled cells with septations in two planes. Sporothrix causes sporotrichosis with asteroid bodies.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with a butterfly-shaped erythematous rash on the cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:640). Anti-dsDNA titre is elevated. Which immunological mechanism most directly causes glomerulonephritis in this patient?
opts: Type III hypersensitivity — immune complex deposition
questions.exp: In SLE, anti-dsDNA antibodies form immune complexes with circulating DNA, which deposit in the glomerular basement membrane and activate complement (Type III hypersensitivity), causing lupus nephritis. This is the most significant cause of morbidity and mortality in SLE.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with small papules coalescing into hypopigmented macules with fine overlying scale on the upper chest and back. KOH preparation shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: The 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern on KOH (short curved hyphae with clusters of spores) is pathognomonic of Pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur (also called M. globosa). The organism produces dicarboxylic acids that inhibit tyrosinase, causing hypopigmentation.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male with history of arsenic exposure presents with arsenical keratoses on palms and soles and multiple pigmented macules (raindrop pigmentation) on the trunk. He is at highest risk of developing which internal malignancy?
opts: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung and bladder
Transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter
Bowen's disease of the skin only
questions.exp: Chronic arsenic exposure causes skin cancer (Bowen's disease, SCC, BCC) and significantly increases risk of lung cancer and bladder cancer (SCC/transitional cell carcinoma). The most common internal malignancies associated with chronic arsenicosis are lung and bladder cancers.

questions.q: A newborn is noted to have a large salmon-pink vascular birthmark covering the right face including the upper eyelid and forehead. The ophthalmologist detects raised IOP. MRI shows ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma. What syndrome does this child have?
questions.exp: Sturge-Weber syndrome is characterised by port-wine stain (naevus flammeus) in V1/V2 trigeminal distribution, ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma (causing epilepsy), and glaucoma. It is caused by somatic GNAQ mutations. The port-wine stain is a capillary vascular malformation.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a recurrent BCC on his nose. Which feature of Mohs surgery makes it the treatment of choice for recurrent facial BCC?
opts: Immediate reconstruction possible under the same anaesthesia
No risk of recurrence after a single stage
questions.exp: The key advantage of Mohs micrographic surgery is that 100% of the peripheral and deep surgical margins are examined in horizontal frozen sections (unlike standard excision with vertical bread-loaf sections which sample <1%). This maximises margin clearance while conserving maximum normal tissue — ideal for face and recurrent tumours.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman on isotretinoin for nodulocystic acne develops severe lower back pain and stiffness worsening with rest. X-ray shows sacroiliac joint sclerosis. Which side effect of isotretinoin is most likely?
opts: Skeletal hyperostosis and premature epiphyseal closure
questions.exp: Isotretinoin (13-cis retinoic acid) causes skeletal hyperostosis, premature epiphyseal closure in growing children, and calcification of ligaments. The sacroiliac changes are part of retinoid-induced skeletal hyperostosis. DISH occurs with chronic use at high doses and is a known skeletal side effect.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman with longstanding poorly controlled RA on methotrexate develops multiple skin-coloured subcutaneous nodules over the elbows and extensor tendons. Biopsy shows necrobiosis with palisading histiocytes. What do these nodules represent?
questions.exp: Rheumatoid nodules occur in ~20-30% of RA patients, typically seropositive (RF+). Histologically they show central fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes and an outer zone of chronic inflammation. Paradoxically, methotrexate can accelerate nodulosis (accelerated nodulosis on MTX).

questions.q: A 20-year-old male from Bihar presents with painless progressive swelling of the scrotum and right leg with rough thickened skin. Peripheral blood smear at midnight shows microfilariae. What is the vector of the causative organism?
questions.exp: Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti causing elephantiasis) is transmitted by Culex quinquefasciatus mosquito in India. Microfilariae exhibit nocturnal periodicity — peak in peripheral blood at midnight corresponding to the vector's feeding time. Anopheles transmits malaria; Aedes transmits dengue/yellow fever; Phlebotomus transmits leishmaniasis.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic skin patches over the right cheek and thickened right great auricular nerve. Slit-skin smear shows no acid-fast bacilli. Lepromin test is strongly positive at 4 weeks. What type of leprosy does she have?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) is characterised by: few well-defined hypopigmented macules/patches with loss of sensation and anhidrosis, thickened peripheral nerves near lesions, negative slit-skin smear (paucibacillary), and strongly positive Mitsuda (lepromin) test — indicating strong cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, calcinosis, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Which antibody is most specifically associated with her condition?
questions.exp: The CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is the limited cutaneous form of systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is the specific marker, present in 70-80% of CREST syndrome. Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse SSc with pulmonary fibrosis.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child develops multiple fluid-filled vesicles with honey-coloured crusting around the mouth and nose, spreading to siblings. Gram stain of vesicle fluid shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most common causative organism in Indian children is:
questions.exp: Impetigo in India is predominantly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (bullous and non-bullous impetigo), unlike Western countries where Streptococcus pyogenes was historically more common. S. aureus produces exfoliative toxins (ET-A, ET-B) targeting desmoglein-1, causing bullous impetigo and staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with a slowly enlarging painless nodule on the right lower eyelid that is pearly white with overlying telangiectasias and a central depression. Which histological finding is pathognomonic?
opts: Peripheral palisading of tumour cells with retraction artefact
Individual cell keratinisation with horn pearls
Pagetoid spread of large cells in epidermis
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artefact (peri-tumoral clefting/shrinkage artefact between tumour island and surrounding stroma) on histology — pathognomonic. Individual cell keratinisation is SCC; pagetoid spread is Paget's disease; acanthosis with clefting is pemphigus.

questions.q: A 35-year-old nurse develops a painful, rapidly enlarging erythematous plaque on the forearm with vesicles after contact with hospital linen. Patch testing later shows positive reaction to formaldehyde at 1% aq. The mechanism of this reaction is:
opts: Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity mediated by sensitised T lymphocytes
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) is a Type IV delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction mediated by hapten-specific CD4+ T cells (TH1) and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells. The allergen (formaldehyde) acts as a hapten, binding to skin proteins. Sensitisation takes 10-14 days; re-exposure elicits the reaction in 48-72 hours (patch test read at 48 and 96 hours).

questions.q: A 62-year-old male presents with a 3-cm irregularly pigmented lesion on the back with areas of regression. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network, irregular streaks, blue-white veil, and regression structures. The most important independent prognostic factor is:
questions.exp: Breslow thickness (measured in mm from the granular cell layer to the deepest tumour cell) is the single most important prognostic factor in melanoma. It directly determines T-staging in AJCC staging and predicts risk of metastasis and survival. Clark's level is no longer used in current AJCC 8th edition staging.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules on the flexor aspects of the wrists and ankles. Oral examination shows white lacy streaks on the buccal mucosa. Wickham's striae are visible on dermoscopy. What is the basic pathology?
opts: Interface dermatitis with lichenoid infiltrate and basal cell vacuolation
questions.exp: Lichen planus shows interface dermatitis — a lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate hugging the dermoepidermal junction with vacuolar degeneration of basal keratinocytes and colloid (Civatte) bodies. Wickham's striae result from focal hypergranulosis. The 6 P's: Purple, Polygonal, Pruritic, Papules, Planar, Peripheral involvement.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male with chronic stable plaque psoriasis is started on methotrexate. Pre-treatment workup should include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pre-MTX workup includes: CBC, LFT, RFT, hepatitis B and C serology, chest X-ray (to rule out TB), and urine pregnancy test in women. Serum uric acid is not part of routine pre-MTX workup. MTX can rarely cause hyperuricaemia as a side effect, but baseline uric acid is not required before starting.

questions.q: A 24-year-old female presents with painful grouped vesicles on the vulva, inguinal lymphadenopathy, dysuria, and fever occurring for the first time. First episode of genital herpes is most commonly caused by:
questions.exp: While both HSV-1 and HSV-2 can cause genital herpes, classical primary genital herpes with severe symptoms (fever, inguinal lymphadenopathy, dysuria) is most commonly caused by HSV-2. However, HSV-1 now accounts for up to 50% of new genital herpes cases in developed countries due to orogenital contact. In India, HSV-2 remains predominant for genital disease.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male presents with macular, papular, and papulosquamous lesions all over the body including palms and soles, with generalised lymphadenopathy and condylomata lata perianally. VDRL titre is 1:128. This represents which stage of syphilis?
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis occurs 6-8 weeks after primary chancre (which may have healed). It presents with diffuse polymorphic rash including palms and soles (pathognomonic), condylomata lata, mucous patches, generalised lymphadenopathy, and constitutional symptoms. VDRL is positive at high titres. Condylomata lata are highly infectious flat warty plaques at mucocutaneous junctions.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman with longstanding SLE is started on hydroxychloroquine. Which ophthalmological complication must be screened annually after 5 years of use?
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine binds to melanin in the RPE of the retina. Long-term use (>5 years or cumulative dose >1000g) can cause bull's eye maculopathy — irreversible retinal toxicity with a central scotoma. Annual ophthalmological screening with macular OCT and visual field testing is recommended after 5 years of use.

questions.q: A 70-year-old female presents with painful grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution along T5 dermatome with post-herpetic neuralgia for 3 months. Which antiviral if started within 72 hours of rash onset most effectively prevents PHN?
questions.exp: Valacyclovir (prodrug of acyclovir with 3-5x higher bioavailability) 1g TDS for 7 days started within 72 hours reduces duration, severity, and risk of post-herpetic neuralgia more effectively than standard acyclovir doses. Famciclovir 500mg TDS is equally effective. Both valacyclovir and famciclovir have superior bioavailability over oral acyclovir.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with scrotal swelling, cauliflower-like warty growths on the penile shaft, and similar lesions perianally. HPV typing of the lesions would most likely show:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11 in ~90% of cases. These types do not integrate into the host genome and rarely cause malignant transformation. High-risk HPV 16 and 18 cause cervical cancer and Bowenoid papulosis. HPV 1 and 2 cause common/plantar warts.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with multiple comedones, milia, and atrophic scars on sun-damaged skin of the temples and periorbital area. She is a chronic pipe smoker. Which condition does she have?
questions.exp: Favre-Racouchot syndrome (nodular elastosis with cysts and comedones) occurs on severely photodamaged skin, particularly periorbital and temporal areas. It is associated with chronic UV exposure and smoking. It presents with open and closed comedones, large cysts, and milia on elastotic skin. Treatment includes retinoids and comedone extraction.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with depigmented macules that are chalk-white, sharply demarcated, with convex margins. Wood's lamp examination shows brilliant white fluorescence enhancing the contrast. DOPA reaction on biopsy shows complete absence of melanocytes. Autoantibodies against which protein are pathogenic?
questions.exp: Vitiligo is caused by immune-mediated destruction of melanocytes. Autoantibodies and cytotoxic CD8+ T cells target melanocyte-specific antigens including tyrosinase, MCHR1 (melanocortin receptor 1), SOX10, and MART-1. The absence of melanocytes on DOPA (negative) staining differentiates vitiligo from pityriasis alba and hypomelanosis of Ito.
